name: Taiwan
summary: Taiwan is not in the EU, so EU, US and other citizens are treated alike. There is no investor residence visa; most routes are discretionary. The cheapest route in practice for a professional is the Employment Gold Card (qualification-based, a salary of NT$160,000 a month is one path), for founders the Entrepreneur Visa, and for remote workers from visa-exempt countries the Digital Nomad Visitor Visa (US$40,000 a year). Permanent residence by investment (reportedly NT$15 million) is approved by the National Immigration Agency.
naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation (Nationality Act art. 3) needs more than 183 days of legal residence a year for at least 5 consecutive years, a domicile in Taiwan and enough property or skills to live on; 3 years for some (art. 4, e.g. spouses of citizens). High-level professionals recommended by the competent ministry need 2 consecutive years (art. 5).
dual_citizenship_note: Applicants must prove they lost their original nationality within one year of approval (art. 9). High-level professionals recommended by the competent authority are exempt (art. 9 para. 4) and keep their original nationality.

routes.limited_places: discretionary: each applicant is reviewed by the competent ministry for their field; no right to the card
routes.fees_note: Fees not sourced from an official page.
routes.processing_time: Typically about 1 to 3 months in total (information check 1-2 weeks, qualification check 1-2 months, card printing 1-2 weeks)
routes.family: Holders can bring family; details not sourced
routes.tax_note: A resident of more than 183 days a year is taxed in Taiwan; the card offers tax benefits for high salaries (conditions apply). A permit does not by itself make you tax resident.
routes.name: Employment Gold Card
routes.summary: A combined residence permit, work permit and re-entry permit for foreign professionals in listed fields (finance, economy, technology, digital, law, education, culture and arts, sport). It lets you work for any employer. Mainland Chinese, Hong Kong/Macau and Taiwanese dual citizens are excluded.
routes.requirements: Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals. Apply online and qualify in one field and sub-category. A monthly salary of at least NT$160,000 (average over a year, before tax, shown on a tax statement or an employment contract for future work in Taiwan) is one qualifying path in some fields (NT$160,000 x 12 = NT$1,920,000 a year); other paths need no salary: a PhD from a top-500 university, a licence as a Taiwan or foreign-law attorney, associate-professor or higher rank, proof of unique talent in technology or the digital field, sport or culture achievements. Sole-proprietor and dividend income does not count. Not open to Mainland Chinese citizens, Hong Kong/Macau and Taiwan dual citizens, stateless persons, or Taiwan household-registered nationals living in Taiwan. The Act was amended (passed 29 August 2025; most provisions in force 1 January 2026, others 30 June 2026); some details here may predate those changes.
routes.physical_presence: Not required to keep the card itself; permanent residence needs an average of more than 183 days a year in Taiwan

routes.limited_places: discretionary: investment and permanent residence must be approved by the National Immigration Agency
routes.investment_options: NT$15 million in a for-profit enterprise with 5 jobs for Taiwanese nationals, or NT$30 million in government bonds/approved fund (secondary sources, unverified)
routes.fees_note: One secondary source reports an NT$10,000 application fee; not confirmed.
routes.name: Permanent residence by investment (Plum Blossom Card, APRC)
routes.summary: The Immigration Act lets the National Immigration Agency approve permanent residence for an investor who invests first and is then granted the right to stay. Secondary sources give NT$15 million in a for-profit company with at least five jobs, or NT$30 million in government bonds; the official amounts were not found.
routes.requirements: Immigration Act art. 25 (investment immigration): application, review and approval by the National Immigration Agency, then the investment is made; the Agency then consents to permanent residence. Spouse and minor children can apply with the investor. The statute text read does not state the amount. Secondary sources (not official): NT$15 million in a for-profit Taiwan enterprise creating at least 5 jobs for Taiwanese nationals, or NT$30 million in government bonds or an approved fund, held for 3 years (one 2012 source says 5 years and a prior ARC of 3 or 5 years). Applicants must be adults of good conduct. Taiwan has no standalone investor visa.
routes.physical_presence: Unclear; secondary sources say no or minimal presence is required

routes.limited_places: discretionary: qualification is examined by the MOEA Investment Commission
routes.name: Entrepreneur Visa
routes.summary: A residence visa for founders of an innovative start-up, examined by the Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission. You qualify through outside funding, an approved incubator, patents or an award, or by having already invested at least NT$1 million in a qualifying Taiwan company.
routes.requirements: Examination Directions of Entrepreneur Visa Qualification for Foreign Nationals: education to at least senior high school level, plus at least one of: venture capital investment or at least NT$2 million from an approved fund-raising platform; admission to an approved innovation park or incubator; a patent; a start-up or design award or approved government project; or an existing innovative company (registered under 5 years) with at least NT$1 million invested, where you are the legal representative. Teams may apply together. The company must then reach a performance test (reported: NT$3 million sales, or three full-time Taiwanese employees) for extension; the validity and extension period was not read from the official text.

routes.limited_places: discretionary: applications are reviewed by the National Development Council
routes.tax_note: Staying more than 183 days in a calendar year makes you tax resident in Taiwan.
routes.name: Digital Nomad Visitor Visa
routes.summary: A visitor visa for remote workers from visa-exempt countries, in effect since 1 January 2025. It is a visitor visa, not a residence permit.
routes.requirements: Only nationals of visa-exempt countries. Proof of remote work (CV or portfolio, a work contract) and a description of intended activities. Either a digital nomad visa from another country, or an annual salary of at least US$40,000 (age 30 and over) or US$20,000 (ages 20 to 29) in one of the last two years. Average monthly bank balance of at least US$10,000 over the last six months. International health insurance covering the whole stay. Apply at a Taiwan overseas mission. Official page shows no maximum stay; secondary sources say up to 6 months.
routes.physical_presence: Visitor stay only; no days required

open_questions: Employment Gold Card fees, permit validity options (official page says up to 3 years; amended Act may allow up to 5), and family rules were not found on an official page.

Gold Card path to permanent residence: official page says 3 years for specialist professionals with an average of over 183 days a year; whether the 2025 Act amendment (in force 1 January and 30 June 2026) shortened this, and any 183-day change, was not confirmed.

Investor APRC: the NT$15 million (5 jobs) and NT$30 million (bonds) amounts and holding period come from secondary sources and disagree on 3 vs 5 years and on any prior ARC; the Immigration Act text read does not state the amount. Fees unsourced.
A reported NT$6 million investor ARC could not be confirmed and is not included.
Entrepreneur Visa: validity, extension tests, fees and family rules not verified from the current official text.
Digital nomad visitor visa: maximum stay, fee and the visa-exempt country list not stated on the official page; a proposed extension to 2 years was not confirmed.
General employer-sponsored work permits (Employment Service Act, Ministry of Labor) were not researched and no route is included for them.
Taiwan's permanent-residence rule for ordinary residents (Immigration Act art. 25: 5 years, 183 days a year) was read, but whether it was changed in 2026 was not checked.
Whether the government processing time for naturalisation and the high-level professional recognition standards changed after the 2024 amendment was not checked.
